comparator.name: International Business Communication
comparator.academicYear: 2026–2027 adopted programme-specific OER; later prospective pages used only for thematic context
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–27 adopted OER, article 5, establishes the IBC English track as 60 EC of twelve required first-year 5-EC courses; 30 EC of six required second-year courses plus 30 EC of permitted minor choice; and 10 EC PPD, 5 EC Cross-cultural language use English, 5 EC Academic and Professional Language Skills English, 30 EC free choice and a 10-EC thesis in year three. Its zero-credit mentorship and RADAr elements are acknowledged but excluded from 180 EC. The prospective pages describe later academic years 2027–30 and give a different first-year grouping and third-year English-track listing (including Misinformation and Persuasion); those are not substituted for the current formal English-track 2026–27 requirements. The optional Spanish language track is not combined with this English track.
components: Restricted choice of permitted Faculty of Arts minors or programme electives, normally two 15-EC minors; no particular optional minor is compulsory.

alternatives.label: Intercultural and strategic business communication
alternatives.concept: Rhetoric, language and media analysis are linked to marketing, organisational leadership, cross-border business and empirical audience research. The curriculum addresses strategic intercultural communication while its film and media studies broaden the channels considered; it cannot reproduce Radboud’s dedicated English-language communication sequence or independent IBC thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed 24-course schedule sustains organisational strategy, rhetoric, intercultural media analysis and audience research.
progression: Every formal prerequisite is in an earlier semester and every course is offered in its assigned semester. Rhetoric, media and sociology foundations precede advanced communication and media analysis where scheduling permits; required PPD is in year one.

alternatives.label: Communication for public and social impact
alternatives.concept: Communication and media courses combine with social-movement studies, civil society, human rights, public health and climate science. Students analyse how persuasion and audiovisual narratives shape public understanding, then ground social-impact messaging in evidence about health, justice and the environment.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed 24-course schedule sustains persuasion with health, environmental and civic social-impact applications.
progression: Every formal prerequisite is in an earlier semester and every course is offered in its assigned semester. Rhetoric, media and sociology foundations precede advanced communication and media analysis where scheduling permits; required PPD is in year one.
alternatives.distinctness: The public-impact curriculum replaces nine courses (67.5 EC) in the closest match with climate communication, public health, human rights, social movements, civic theory and youth-resilience research. The changed courses implement the explicit social-impact and health-communication direction.

alternatives.label: Digital communication and audience analytics
alternatives.concept: Rhetoric, media and business strategy combine with programming, data science, machine learning, statistics and AI ethics. The curriculum studies digital audiences and communication technologies through both critical media analysis and direct computational work.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed 24-course schedule sustains digital media research with a substantial programming, data and AI sequence.
progression: Every formal prerequisite is in an earlier semester and every course is offered in its assigned semester. Rhetoric, media and sociology foundations precede advanced communication and media analysis where scheduling permits; required PPD is in year one.
alternatives.distinctness: The programming, mathematics, data, machine-learning and AI-ethics sequence changes both method and subject. This curriculum differs from the management route by seven courses (52.5 EC) and from the social-impact route by thirteen (97.5 EC), reflecting the evidenced human-and-digital direction.

routeSelection.basis: The generic target names the English-taught International Business Communication specialisation. The adopted OER offers English and optional Spanish language tracks; English is the broad default without an added Spanish-language requirement. The three thematic profiles are possible academic directions, not a reason to replace the formal English-track curriculum or prefill 30 EC of minor and 30 EC of free electives.

selection.assessment: The closest management, language and research route is followed by evidenced social-impact and people-and-digital directions. Each has a coherent and feasible distinct curriculum, while Spanish is independently assessed and rejected for lack of any Spanish language sequence at UCR. Three is the maximum.

notes.text: The comparison uses Radboud’s adopted 2026–27 International Business Communication English track. Its minor and free-elective spaces remain choices; its language-skill courses and 10-EC thesis are distinct requirements. UCR courses in rhetoric, business, media and quantitative research offer useful intersections but do not confer English-language proficiency credits or an IBC thesis.
